items.summary: The Hechyeomoyeo (HCMY) opened its 18th mass exhibition at KOTE in central Seoul's Insa-dong on Wednesday. The opening party featured music, live drawing, face painting, clowns and flash tattoos, as art lovers from Korea and all around the world crowded into all five floors plus the roof and basement of the aging building that houses KOTE. “My approach is straightforward: If someone tells me they have a creative skill to share, I try to find a place for them in the event,” Neil Wheelock Deforest Smith, the American artist who started HCMY, told The Korea Times. HCMY is an independent art initiative that began in Korea as an effort to make exhibition opportunities more accessible to Korea-based artists. It has grown into an international community, connecting hundreds of creators across continents. Despite its global reach, HCMY maintains a strong connection to its Korean roots. Smith estimates that approximately 65 percent of the participants at HCMY's Korean exhibitions are Korean nationals, while around 20 to 30 percent are foreign residents, and the rest are international artists

items.summary: RIYADH — The Transport General Authority (TGA) has announced an extension of up to six months to the operational lifespan of vehicles used in taxi services and private car rentals, extending the deadline to June 30, 2027. The decision applies to vehicles whose permitted operational lifespan expires at the end of 2026, allowing establishments to continue using them for an additional period. The decision also seeks to help establishments maximize the use of their existing vehicles and improve operational efficiency. The TGA emphasized that the measure forms part of its ongoing efforts to develop the regulatory environment for transport activities, enhance service sustainability and support the sector’s long-term growth.

items.summary: MAKKAH — The Muslim World League (MWL) has strongly condemned the Houthi militia’s continued attempts to target Muslim holy sites in Makkah and Madinah, as well as civilian areas across Saudi Arabia. In a statement issued by its General Secretariat, MWL Secretary-General and Chairman of the Organization of Muslim Scholars Sheikh Dr. Mohammed Al-Issa denounced the militia’s deliberate attacks using ballistic missiles and drones, which were successfully intercepted by Saudi air defenses, describing them as violations of the sanctity of holy sites and innocent lives. Al-Issa warned that the attacks risk provoking the sentiments of more than two billion Muslims, condemning the militia’s repeated acts of terrorism and violations of religious and humanitarian principles. He stressed that the actions of the group calling itself Ansar Allah constitute a betrayal of religion and Muslims and contradict the guidance of God and His Messenger. Speaking on behalf of the MWL’s councils, bodies and international assemblies, Al-Issa reaffirmed full solidarity with Saudi Arabia in all measures taken to deter the attackers and protect holy sites and innocent lives. He concluded by praying for the Kingdom’s continued security and the protection of its leadership and people.

items.summary: BRUSSELS — Saudi Arabia has provided more than $145 billion in humanitarian assistance to 175 countries worldwide, according to Dr. Abdullah Al Rabeeah, Advisor at the Royal Court and Supervisor General of the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief). During his virtual participation in a World Economic Forum session titled “A New Ambition for Fragile and Frontier Markets” in Brussels, Belgium, Al Rabeeah highlighted that KSrelief has implemented over 4,000 projects worth more than $8.5 billion across 113 countries. Al Rabeeah called for a shift in how fragile and frontier markets are perceived, emphasizing their potential for locally led economic growth and sustainable resilience rather than continued dependence on humanitarian assistance. **media[2790633]** He outlined three priorities to support this transformation: upholding international humanitarian law and ensuring safe, unhindered humanitarian access; strengthening locally led relief efforts without placing additional burdens on communities; and mobilizing innovative financing to address growing funding gaps. He stressed that grants alone are insufficient, calling for greater use of public financing, blended finance, risk-sharing mechanisms and private capital to encourage investment in high-risk frontier markets. Al Rabeeah concluded by urging stronger international cooperation to transform humanitarian relief into long-term resilience and shared prosperity, creating opportunities while preserving the dignity of vulnerable communities.

items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development has urged sports centers and gyms to complete employment requirements ahead of the November 18 localization deadline, with two weeks remaining. The ministry called on establishments to ensure their readiness and complete the necessary employment requirements before the decision takes effect. The decision comes as part of ongoing efforts to localize specialized professions in the private sector, with the Ministry of Sport responsible for overseeing its implementation in line with labor market needs. Private sector establishments will also benefit from support programs and incentives provided by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development and its affiliated entities. These include support for recruitment, training, qualification, employment and job retention, alongside priority access to localization support programs and initiatives offered by the Human Resources Development Fund (HRDF), known as Hadaf. Establishments are encouraged to consult the official procedural guide for further details on the requirements and implementation process.

items.summary: RIYADH — The General Directorate of Civil Defense has urged the public to exercise caution and remain in safe locations amid forecasts of thunderstorms hitting across Saudi Arabia from Friday through Tuesday. items.summary: RIYADH — Riyadh Metro, overseen by the Royal Commission for Riyadh City (RCRC), has been named among the world's top four transport projects at the Smart City Expo World Congress 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. The recognition came amid global competition involving 533 entries from 68 countries, marking a new international achievement that reflects Riyadh's leadership in developing modern and sustainable mobility systems.The ranking recognizes the project's scale and advanced technology as one of the world's largest and most modern public transport projects. Riyadh Metro is a key pillar of a sustainable, environmentally friendly urban transport system that contributes to reducing carbon emissions, improving traffic flow and mobility, and accommodating Riyadh's population growth and rapid urban expansion.During its participation, the commission is showcasing the use of data and modern technologies in city planning and management through the Riyadh Data Hub, digital twin applications, and artificial intelligence. It is also highlighting Riyadh's experience in developing its public transport systemand managing traffic, the Green Riyadh program's efforts, and the capital's major development projects.The congress is one of the leading international gatherings focused on urban development and envisioning the future of cities. This year's edition is held under the theme "Urban Solutions, Real Impact," bringing together more than 600 international speakers to discuss the latest solutions and experiences in digital transformation, mobility, energy, environment, housing, and infrastructure. It also aims to strengthen cooperation to build more efficient and sustainable cities.
